subject: ba
title: Business Ethics and Corporate Governance
objectives: Define business ethics, integrity, and identify the causes of unethical managerial behaviour.
Apply the five basic approaches to ethical decision-making.
Define corporate governance and explain its 'four Ps' framework.
Evaluate the need for, codes of, and sanctions within corporate governance in Nigeria.
study:
Ethics are the accepted principles of right or wrong governing the conduct of a person, a profession, or an organisation. Business Ethics specifically concerns truth, justice, fair competition, advertising, social responsibility and corporate behaviour, both at home and abroad. An ethical dilemma arises when none of the available alternatives seems ethically acceptable to the decision maker.

Key termCauses of unethical managerial behaviour — personal ethics, flawed decision-making processes, organisational culture, unrealistic performance expectations, and leadership that sets (or fails to set) the ethical tone.

Five approaches guide ethical decision-making. The Rights Approach (Kant) says an action is right only if it respects everyone's moral rights, treating people as ends, not merely means. The Utilitarian Approach (Bentham and Mill) says the ethical action provides the greatest good for the greatest number. The Virtue Approach focuses on character traits like honesty and integrity that let us develop our human potential. The Fairness/Justice Approach, rooted in Aristotle, holds that equals should be treated equally and unequals unequally. The Common Good Approach asks whether social policies and institutions benefit the whole community. Businesses manage ethics practically through codes of conduct, ethics training, ethics officers, whistle-blowing mechanisms, and leadership by example.

Exam tipMatch each approach to its founding philosopher when studying: Rights → Kant, Utilitarian → Bentham/Mill, Fairness/Justice → Aristotle. Exam questions frequently test this pairing directly.

Corporate Governance, per the OECD (2004), is the system by which business corporations are directed and controlled — distributing rights and responsibilities among the board, managers, shareholders and other stakeholders. It's often pictured as a three-legged stool: senior management, the board of directors, and shareholders. Governance failures carry real consequences — the 2001 Enron accounting scandal is the textbook cautionary example. Governance is often summarised as the '4 Ps': People, Performance, Processes and Policies.

Corporate compliance is distinct from governance: if governance sets the guiding principles, compliance is the practical work of meeting the legal and regulatory requirements dictated by a firm's industry, activities and jurisdiction. Good governance practice includes ensuring director independence (so decisions stay forward-looking, not just conservative), auditor independence (protecting the trustworthiness of financial reporting), and transparency (reporting bad news as readily as good news). In Nigeria, sector regulators — the SEC, the CBN (for banks), and NAICOM (for insurance) — each issue their own governance codes. Non-compliance can bring regulatory fines, suspension from trading, and removal of erring directors. A Social Audit complements financial audits by evaluating a firm's performance against its social responsibility objectives and stakeholder expectations.
recap:
• Ethics = accepted principles of right/wrong; ethical dilemma = no acceptable alternative exists.
  • Unethical behaviour causes: personal ethics, decision processes, culture, performance pressure, leadership.
  • Five ethical approaches: Rights (Kant) · Utilitarian (Bentham/Mill – greatest good) · Virtue (character) · Fairness/Justice (Aristotle) · Common Good (community benefit).
  • Corporate Governance (OECD) = system directing/controlling corporations; 'three-legged stool' of management, board, shareholders; 4 Ps: People, Performance, Processes, Policies.
  • Governance = guiding principles; Compliance = practical legal/regulatory adherence.
  • Nigeria's sector regulators: SEC, CBN (banks), NAICOM (insurance). Sanctions: fines, trading suspension, director removal.
  • Social Audit: evaluates performance against social responsibility objectives.

quiz.q: Ethics is best described as:
opts: Only relevant to government employees
A synonym for corporate tax law
A legally binding contract between two parties
Accepted principles of right or wrong governing the conduct of a person, profession or organisation

quiz.q: Business Ethics is described as concerned with truth, justice, fair competition and:
opts: Only the company's advertising jingles
Only the company's product packaging
Only interest rates on business loans
Advertising, public relations, social responsibilities and corporate behaviour

quiz.q: An Ethical Dilemma is best described as a situation in which:
opts: Ethics play no role whatsoever in the decision
There is only one possible course of action with no choice involved
None of the available alternatives seems ethically acceptable to the decision maker
Every available alternative is perfectly and equally ethical

quiz.q: Which of the following is identified as a cause of unethical managerial behaviour?
opts: Personal ethics, decision-making processes, organisational culture, unrealistic performance expectations and leadership
Overwhelming employee loyalty
Excessive government regulation with no exception
Too much transparency in financial reporting

quiz.q: The Rights Approach to ethical decision-making is rooted in the philosophy of:
opts: Jeremy Bentham exclusively
John Rawls exclusively
Immanuel Kant
Aristotle exclusively

quiz.q: The Utilitarian Approach, conceived by Bentham and Mill, holds that the ethical action is the one that:
opts: Is determined solely by legal requirement
Benefits only the decision maker personally
Ignores the consequences of the action entirely
Provides the greatest good for the greatest number

quiz.q: The Virtue Approach to ethics focuses on:
opts: Attitudes, dispositions or character traits (such as honesty and integrity) that enable us to develop our human potential
Only the financial outcome of a decision
The complete rejection of all personal character development
Only strict legal compliance with no moral dimension

quiz.q: The Fairness (Justice) Approach is rooted in the teaching of which ancient philosopher?
opts: John Stuart Mill
Jeremy Bentham
Aristotle
Immanuel Kant

quiz.q: The Common Good Approach to ethics focuses on ensuring that social policies and institutions are:
opts: Beneficial to only a select few individuals
Entirely irrelevant to community welfare
Designed to benefit only the government
Beneficial to all members of the community

opts: Only the process of hiring new employees
A synonym for corporate marketing strategy
The system by which business corporations are directed and controlled
A purely voluntary set of suggestions with no formal structure

opts: The media exclusively
Shareholders
Competing companies
Foreign governments

Enron
Apple

quiz.q: The 4 Ps of Corporate Governance are People, Performance, Processes and:

Profit

quiz.q: Corporate Compliance, as distinguished from Corporate Governance, refers to:
opts: Only marketing strategy formulation
Only employee recruitment procedures
The same exact concept as corporate governance with no distinction whatsoever
Meeting a company's legal and regulatory requirements as dictated by industry, activities and jurisdiction

quiz.q: Ensuring 'director independence', as a corporate governance best practice, is important because it:
opts: Enables forward-looking decision-making rather than conservative, safe thinking
Eliminates the need for a board of directors entirely
Has no bearing on innovation or decision quality
Guarantees directors will always agree with management on every decision

quiz.q: Ensuring 'auditor independence' is important for corporate governance primarily because it:
opts: Eliminates the need for financial statements entirely
Protects the accuracy and trustworthiness of a company's financial reporting
Has no relevance to investor confidence
Guarantees auditors will always approve management's decisions

quiz.q: 'Being transparent', as a corporate governance best practice, requires organisations to:
opts: Accurately report both good and bad news to stakeholders
Report only positive news and conceal negative developments
Only disclose information to competitors
Avoid any communication with shareholders whatsoever

quiz.q: In Nigeria, corporate governance codes have been issued by sector regulators including SEC, CBN and:
opts: Only religious institutions
NAICOM (for the insurance sector)
Only the Ministry of Sports
Only foreign regulatory bodies with no domestic relevance

quiz.q: Sanctions for non-compliance with corporate governance codes can include:
opts: Automatic increase in the company's stock price
Guaranteed government subsidy
Regulatory fines, suspension of trading, and removal of erring directors
Complete exemption from all future regulation

quiz.q: A Social Audit in corporate governance primarily evaluates:
opts: Only the company's cash balance at year end
An organisation's performance against its social responsibility objectives and stakeholder expectations
Only the founder's personal net worth
Only the price of the company's raw materials
